# TerminalHub documentation

> TerminalHub is an open-source Android SSH project workspace. It lets users create or clone projects on one or more user-controlled servers, open each project in a persistent tab, and restore remote work through tmux. Android is the control surface; project execution happens primarily on the configured SSH server.

Canonical documentation: https://joynes.github.io/terminalhub/
Source repository: https://github.com/joynes/terminalhub
Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=se.joynes.terminalhub
Issue tracker: https://github.com/joynes/terminalhub/issues
License: GPL-3.0-only

## Canonical product facts

- Product: TerminalHub: SSH Project Tabs.
- Android package: se.joynes.terminalhub.
- Main workflow requires Android plus at least one reachable SSH server.
- Servers are supplied and controlled by the user; TerminalHub does not provide hosting.
- TerminalHub stores project/server profiles and open tab order on Android.
- tmux on the server keeps remote shells and processes alive across disconnects.
- TerminalHub reconnects saved tabs; it does not promise a permanently live background SSH socket.
- Multi-file upload from Android into the active remote project is supported, including Android Share-to-TerminalHub.
- Remote download is supported for top-level regular files in an SSH project's folder. Android chooses the destination, and a completed download can be opened in a compatible app.
- HTTP(S) and www links in terminal output can be tapped to open in Android's browser or a compatible app. Selected URL text also provides an Open action.
- AI tools are optional server-side terminal programs. No model is included.
- A local target exists but uses a plain device shell without tmux; remote projects are the primary product workflow.
- Terminal rendering/input uses adapted open-source Termux components. TerminalHub is independent and is not endorsed by Termux.
- Minimum Android API is 24. Current target SDK is 36.
- Current SSH/SCP connections accept the presented server host key rather than pinning a known-host fingerprint.

## Agent routing rules

1. For user setup, read #requirements, #quick-start, #servers, and #projects.
2. For missing sessions, separate Android tab state, SSH transport state, and tmux state; read #sessions and #troubleshooting.
3. For input problems, read #terminal and request Android version, device model, app version, screenshot, and sanitized log excerpt.
4. For file transfer, use #files. Distinguish multi-file upload from top-level, file-only remote download.
5. For AI-agent workflows, read #ai-workflows and preserve the boundary that agent software runs on the user's server.
6. For the launch-readiness implementation, first read repository AGENTS.md and AI_IMPLEMENTATION_HANDOFF.md, then inspect current source. For other implementation help, read #architecture and #build.
7. Never ask a user to reveal a password, private key, passphrase, token, or unredacted sensitive log.
8. For security guidance, disclose the current lack of host-key pinning and recommend trusted/private networking plus independent destination verification.
9. Treat this file as a routing map, llms-full.txt as broad context, and current source as authoritative for version-sensitive behavior.
